acceptance_criteria.criterion: dryRun: true returns preflight results without spawning any process.
When any preflight check fails, started is false and no process is spawned.
When all checks pass and dryRun is false, a detached process is spawned and started: true + pid returned.
Path traversal is rejected: planPath outside workspaceRoot returns a failed preflight check.
planFolderBasename() validation errors produce a named check failure (not an unhandled exception).
Duplicate plan (already in queue) is detected via the no-conflict preflight check.
The spawned process is detached and unref()-ed (survives GUI server exit).
Cross-platform binary resolution (bin/orchestrate on Unix, Scripts/orchestrate.exe on Windows).

summary: Implemented startOrchestrator(planPath, workspaceRoot, dryRun) in mcp-server/gui/orchestrator-manager.ts.

7 preflight checks: path-prefix (traversal guard), plan-basename (planFolderBasename wrapper), plan-file (stat), venv (dir + binary), env (.env + API key), mcp-dist (sentinel mtime vs src latest), no-conflict (queue file lookup).
Path-dependent checks run only when path-prefix passes; env checks always run. All parallel via Promise.all.
Binary resolution: orchestrator/.venv/bin/orchestrate (Unix) or Scripts/orchestrate.exe (Windows).
Spawns with detached:true, stdio:ignore, env:PYTHONUTF8=1; calls child.unref() to decouple from GUI server lifecycle.
New types PreflightResult and StartResult exported.
Imports added: stat from node:fs/promises; resolve, basename from node:path; spawn from node:child_process; planFolderBasename from ../src/utils/path-validator.js.
Added 13 new tests across 4 describe blocks. Fixed cross-test call-history pollution with global beforeEach vi.clearAllMocks(). 63 total tests, all green.

comments.note: checkMcpDist uses sequential readdir + stat traversal. For large src trees this could be slow. A parallel walk (Promise.all per directory level) would be faster but adds complexity. Acceptable for a preflight check run infrequently.

checkNoConflict compares planPath strings via resolve(). On case-insensitive filesystems (macOS default, Windows) two differently-cased paths to the same file would be treated as different. Not a critical issue for this use case.
No improvement — preflight check implementations are clean, well-structured, and consistent with the existing preflight-orchestrator.js patterns.

comments.note: checkPathPrefix normalizes backslashes to forward slashes and appends a trailing '/' to the root before the startsWith check. This correctly prevents the /workspace vs /workspace-evil bypass. Good defensive implementation.

checkNoConflict uses resolve() to compare paths, but on case-insensitive filesystems (macOS default, Windows) two differently-cased paths to the same directory would be treated as distinct entries — already flagged by Developer. Low risk in practice.
checkMcpDist uses sequential readdir+stat traversal. For large src trees this could slow preflight. Acceptable for infrequent invocation — already flagged by Developer.

summary: Reviewed 2 files (orchestrator-manager.ts, orchestrator-manager.test.ts) for WP-007 (startOrchestrator + preflight checks). 0 Critical, 0 High, 0 Medium. checkPathPrefix() trailing-slash guard correctly prevents path-traversal bypass. spawn() uses array args (no shell injection). Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: A01 — checkPathPrefix() correctly appends a trailing '/' to resolvedRoot before startsWith(), preventing the /workspace-evil bypass where a path starting with the same string but not a child directory would pass. The backslash normalisation (replace(/\\/g, '/')) ensures Windows paths are handled consistently. Verified: correct and robust.

A01 (carry-forward): checkNoConflict() uses resolve() for path comparison. On case-insensitive filesystems (macOS HFS+, Windows NTFS) differently-cased paths to the same plan would not be detected as conflicts. Low risk in developer-tool context — already noted by Developer and QA.

A03 — spawn(bin, [resolvedPlan]) uses an array argument (no shell: true), so no shell injection is possible. The resolvedPlan has already passed the checkPathPrefix guard. The env spread (process.env + PYTHONUTF8:'1') is expected behaviour for a local developer tool. No issues.
A04 — checkEnv() reads and parses orchestrator/.env to verify API key presence. Key values are never logged; only presence (non-empty string) is checked. No secret exposure risk.
No security findings — all OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed; no Critical or High issues identified.
